title: Polymorphism and duck typing
learningGoals: call the same method on different objects
recognise an AttributeError from a missing method

youtube.title: Python Polymorphism and Duck Typing | Python Programming EP 69
youtube.description: In this episode you will call the same method on different objects, explain duck typing and recognise an AttributeError from a missing method, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Same call, many shapes · 1:00 One loop, many shapes · 1:40 One list, different objects · 2:13 Second program · 3:13 Recap · 3:44 Bug of the Day · 4:32 Challenge · 4:52 Next episode

scenes.narration: One loop, many kinds of objects, each doing its own thing. That is polymorphism.

scenes.onScreen: "Same call, many shapes": three numbered lines (1. Polymorphism: one call, many behaviours; 2. Python does not check the class, only the method; 3. If it quacks like a duck, treat it as a duck) and an analogy card: a remote with a play button: it works on any device that knows how to play, whatever the brand
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: Polymorphism means many shapes. You call the same method on different objects, and each one responds in its own way. Python goes further. It does not check the class at all. It only asks, does this object have the method I am calling? This is called duck typing. If it walks like a duck, and quacks like a duck, treat it as a duck. Think of a remote with a play button. It works on any device that knows how to play.

scenes.onScreen: shapes.py: different classes with the same area method
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right; faint indent guide lines
scenes.narration: [HL 1] A Square class. [HL 2] Init stores the side. [HL 5] Its area method. [HL 6] Side times side. [HL 8] A Circle class. [HL 9] Init stores the radius. [HL 12] Its own area method. [HL 13] Pi times radius squared, rounded. [HL 15] A list with different kinds of shapes. [HL 16] Loop over them. [HL 17] The same call, shape dot area, on every object. Square nine. Circle twelve point five seven. Square sixteen. No class check anywhere.

scenes.onScreen: The name shapes tied to a list holding two Square objects and a Circle object
scenes.animation: Name tags pop in with their arrows to the objects (value and type shown, no addresses); when Python reads a name the arrow glows and the object lights up
scenes.narration: Here is the picture. The name shapes is tied to one list. Inside the list sit three objects, two squares and a circle. The classes are unrelated, there is no parent class at all. But all three know area, so the loop works. Python cares only about what an object can do, not what it is called.

scenes.onScreen: ducks.py: a function that works with any object that has speak

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One: Polymorphism: the same call behaves differently on different objects. Two: Python checks only that the method exists. Three: That is duck typing: if it quacks, treat it as a duck. Four: Use hasattr to test for a method. Pause the video, and say these ideas out loud, once, slowly.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: calling a missing method
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. The talk function calls speak, but our Robot only has a method named beep. Python finds out at the moment of the call. Attribute error, Robot object has no attribute speak. Duck typing needs every object to offer the method that the function calls.

props.error:
File "talk.py", line 6, in talk
    return thing.speak()
           ^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'Robot' object has no attribute 'speak'
props.why: Duck typing only works if the object really has the method you call. Python finds out when the call happens, and raises an AttributeError.

shorts.title: Many shapes
shorts.script: Polymorphism means many shapes. You call the same method on different objects, and each answers in its own way. Square area, circle area, triangle area. One loop, one call, three different calculations. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: One call, many behaviours.

shorts.title: Duck typing
shorts.hook: "Python does not ask, what class are you?"
shorts.script: Python does not ask, what class are you? It asks, do you have the method I want to call? If it walks like a duck, and quacks like a duck, treat it as a duck. The class does not matter at all. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.onScreen: if it quacks, it is a duck
shorts.caption: Python trusts methods.

shorts.title: No parent needed
shorts.hook: "Notice that Square and Circle share no parent class."
shorts.script: Notice that Square and Circle share no parent class. They are unrelated. Yet one loop works on both, because both have an area method. Duck typing needs no inheritance. Just the right method name. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Only the method matters.

shorts.title: Missing method
shorts.hook: "What if an object lacks the method?"
shorts.script: What if an object lacks the method? Calling thing dot speak on a robot that only has beep raises, attribute error, Robot object has no attribute speak. You can test first with hasattr, or just make sure every class offers the method. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Try it in your own file and watch what happens. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Check the method name.
